Figure 1:Context-centric streaming versus supervising the visible
state.Top:recent-frame models see little history and
history-centric models leave temporal composition implicit; both inherit
answer-level supervision, whereas we supervise the visible state and acquire
causal views on demand.Bottom:counting movie inserts, the recent
view misses earlier ones and historical sampling skips the first; retrieving it restores the count. This example does not separate the two levers.

Figure 2:Overview.Phase 1, ViSS
(Section4.1):probes of event identity,
order, accumulation, and relation change (illustrated), together with sufficiency, train a shared
representation in one epoch; recent-4 is the dominant training input and the
evaluation interface (longer views: AppendixB.3).Phase 2, TVS (Section4.2):the checkpoint is
frozen; the event view is acquired when the recent margin is low, the history
view when the two disagree, and a calibrated margin rule keeps one proposal.

Figure 4:One query per lever. Left: same four recent frames, two checkpoints
(control checkpoint: B, ViSS: A). Right: one frozen ViSS checkpoint, three
causal views; margins in parentheses, full trace in Figure5.

Figure 5:Qualitative case study of causal view acquisition and proposal
commitment. Recent-4 omits the event in which the cat takes the teddy bear and
proposes D. The event view exposes the decisive evidence and proposes A; the
compact-history view independently supports A, which the acquire–commit
policy preserves.

Figure 6:Corrective historical evidence is not accessed.Four actual frames per view are displayed; complete inputs contain 4 recent,
20 event, and 6 history frames. Earlier frames show all three paintings,
while recent-4 loses the left neighbour. All proposals use the same frozen
ViSS checkpoint; only recent-4 is executed by TVS.

Figure 7:All-view failure with ambiguity about what to count.Four actual frames per view are displayed; complete inputs contain 4 recent,
20 event, and 21 history frames. The same frozen ViSS checkpoint is used
throughout. Exact traces for both cases are provided insupplementary/viss_failure_cases.json; no new proposals are generated.

Figure 8:Accumulating movie insertions.At 242 seconds, the recent-frame
control predicts two insertions and the historical-search control predicts
three. Historical sampling omits the first insertion block. Our causal-access
run exposes this missing evidence and returns four, matching the reference.
Each insertion block may contain several consecutive film excerpts.

Figure 9:Following the current lesson topic.The observed lesson moves
from perimeter to area and area formulas. Both controls predict rectangle
perimeter (A), while our run predicts the annotated triangle-area option (D).
The displayed prefix establishes the current area topic; no future frames
are exposed to the model.
